reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific mechanistic claims about strain-induced segregation, phase formation, and toughness reduction in HEAs, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support any of these premises.
premises: Mechanical loading enhances atomic mobility locally in high-entropy alloys
Strain-induced elemental segregation occurs at grain boundaries in initially single-phase HEAs
Segregation leads to formation of brittle intermetallic-like phases at grain boundaries
Grain boundary brittle phases reduce fracture toughness and promote brittle fracture
A critical stress/cycle threshold exists above which this process activates
